findings.issue: FastMCP coerces boolean start_seconds/end_seconds to floats before normalize_file_references runs, bypassing its explicit boolean rejection. A tools/call with False/True succeeds with the invented range 0.0-1.0; use strict numeric input fields and test the registered protocol handler.

Manifest binding defaults index-only references to kind=segment and never checks mime_type. An image/jpeg reference, including one claiming an MP4 filename, is counted and announced as a received MP4. Classify index-only JPEGs as previews, require a manifest preview, and reject MIME/kind conflicts.

The new exact-name lookup rejects preview ResourceLink names emitted by prepare_video_for_chatgpt: tool_result names them preview-0.jpg while the manifest contains preview_000.jpg. A host preserving the advertised resource name fails even with the correct segment_index. Emit the manifest filename and test the producer-to-ingestion round trip.

needs-human: Issue #23 requires a real ChatGPT file reference, a visually verified preview, and per-segment MP4 summaries when supported. This receipt checks supplied metadata and the current widget does not invoke native ingestion; synthetic files.example references and offline tests do not demonstrate those acceptance criteria. Obtain a real host/model receipt or explicitly approve narrowing the issue scope; do not treat the PR's checked acceptance mapping as end-to-end completion.

summary: Fixed all three code defects with failing-before-fix regression tests: boolean timestamp coercion, JPEG/MP4 misclassification, and incompatible preview resource names. Git Bash validation passed: 138 Python tests and 21 widget scenarios, with 2 Linux/WSL-only tests skipped. needs-human: actual ChatGPT attachment delivery, visible-frame verification, and supported MP4 summaries remain unverified against issue #23.
